arxiv-1904-07976.creator: Asim Darwaish, Farid Naït-Abdesselam, Ashfaq Khokhar
arxiv-1904-07976.description: Abstract Intricating cardiac complexities are the primary factor associated with healthcare costs and the highest cause of death rate in the world. arxiv-2110-05653.creator: Bill Poirier
arxiv-2110-05653.description: Abstract The exponential and Gaussian functions are among the most fundamental and important operations, appearing ubiquitously throughout all areas of science, engineering, and mathematics. Whereas formally, it is well-known that any function may in principle be realized on a quantum computer, in practice present-day algorithms tend to be very expensive.

arxiv-2306-14418.title: Context-Encoded Code Change Representation for Automated Commit Message Generation
arxiv-2306-14418.creator: Thanh Trong Vu, Thanh-Dat Do, and Hieu Dinh Vo
arxiv-2306-14418.description: Abstract Changes in source code are an inevitable part of software development. They are the results of indispensable activities such as fixing bugs or improving functionality. Descriptions for code changes (commit messages) help people better understand the changes. However, due to a lack of motivation and time pressure, writing high-quality commit messages remains reluctantly considered.

arxiv-2406-14567.description: Abstract High-quality motion reconstruction that follows the user’s movements can be achieved by high-end mocap systems with many sensors. However, obtaining such animation quality with fewer input devices is gaining popularity as it brings mocap closer to the general public.

arxiv-2503-12932.title: Efficient Action-Constrained Reinforcement Learning via Acceptance-Rejection Method and Augmented MDPs
arxiv-2503-12932.creator: Wei Hung, Shao-Hua Sun, Ping-Chun Hsieh
arxiv-2503-12932.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Wei Hung, Shao-Hua Sun, Ping-Chun Hsieh. Action-constrained reinforcement learning (ACRL) is a generic framework for learning control policies with zero action constraint violation, which is required by various safety-critical and resource-constrained applications. The existing ACRL methods can typically achieve favorable constraint satisfaction but at the cost of either a high computational burden incurred by the quadratic programs (QP) or increased architectural complexity due to the use of sophisticated generative models.

arxiv-2510-01284.title: Ovi: Twin backbone cross-modal fusion for audio-video generation
arxiv-2510-01284.creator: Chetwin Low, Weimin Wang, Calder Katyal
arxiv-2510-01284.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chetwin Low, Weimin Wang, Calder Katyal. Audio–video (AV) generation has often relied on complex multi-stage architectures or sequential synthesis of sound and visuals. We introduce Ovi , a unified paradigm for audio–video generation that models the two modalities as a single generative process. By using blockwise cross-modal fusion of twin-DiT modules, Ovi achieves natural synchronization and removes the need for separate pipelines or post hoc alignment.

pmc-11299107.title: False lumen embolization and false lumen stent-graft techniques for ruptured post-dissection thoracoabdominal aneurysm
pmc-11299107.creator: Takumi Umibe, Hironobu Nishiori, Hiroki Ikeuchi, Shintaroh Koizumi, Hideki Ueda, Goro Matsumiya
pmc-11299107.description: This report details the successful endovascular repair of a ruptured thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm in a patient with chronic type B aortic dissection. The procedure consisted of thoracic endovascular aortic repair, abdominal endovascular aortic repair, false lumen (FL) embolization with Candy-Plug, and FL stent-graft technique. The approach effectively regulated FL inflow, achieving complete FL closure.

pmc-11435226.title: Preparation of N-Halamine Gelatin Sponge and Its Application in the Treatment of Skin Infection
pmc-11435226.creator: Jiahao Zhu, Jiageng Xue, Huaiying Qin, Yiqing Wang, Yefan Wang, Yidan Cheng, Yingxia Ma, Xiaoyun Zhang, Chenliang Gong, Guanghui Zhao, Chi-Jung Chang, Paula C Ferreira, Patrícia Alves
pmc-11435226.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Nowadays, there has been an increasing research interest into N-halamine compounds due to their wide antimicrobial properties and no drug resistance. Most of the research mainly focuses on small molecular N-halamines, while few studies are on macromolecule N-halamines. In this work, antibacterial N-halamine polymer materials based on proteins (GS-Cl) were synthesized with an antibacterial component of oxidative chlorine, a support component of a gelatin sponge.

pmc-11489948.title: Altered trace elements, antioxidant vitamin C, and malondialdehyde levels are associated with the pathophysiology and development of pre-hepatic jaundice: A case-control study
pmc-11489948.creator: Syed Masudur Rahman Dewan, Abhijit Das, Zahra Labiba Ahmed, Sakif Ahamed Khan, Rehnuma Nasim, Md Shahid Sarwar, Mohammad Safiqul Islam, Md Rabiul Islam
pmc-11489948.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Objectives:Pre-hepatic jaundice results from an imbalance between bilirubin production and clearance, often linked to hemoglobinopathies. Antioxidant vitamin C, malondialdehyde, and trace elements play roles in jaundice, yet their specific associations remain unclear. The objective is to assess and compare these biomarkers in pre-hepatic jaundice patients and healthy controls, aiming to identify potential diagnostic markers and understand distinctive characteristics related to the disease’s pathogenesis.Methods:This case–control study enrolled 50 pre-hepatic jaundice patients and 50 healthy controls, utilizing advanced techniques for biomarker quantification.

pmc-11710095.creator: Tiffany A Walker, Jannah Elchommali, Jenny E Han, Alexander Truong, Ihab Hajjar, Felicia Goldstein
pmc-11710095.description: BackgroundAfrican Americans (AA) are disproportionately affected by Long COVID, highlighting the need for targeted research to understand the enduring consequences of COVID‐19 within this community. pmc-12565029.title: EZH2-Mediated PTEN Silencing Promotes AKT-Dependent Afatinib Resistance in Radiation-Resistant Cervical Cancer Cells
pmc-12565029.creator: Won-Hyoek Lee, Seong Cheol Kim, Sungchan Park, Jeong Woo Park, Sang-Hun Lee, Konstantinos A Zikopoulos
pmc-12565029.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Radiation-acquired HeLaR cervical cancer cells exhibit significant afatinib resistance.EZH2 epigenetically silences PTEN, leading to sustained AKT activation. What is the implication of the main findings? Pharmacologic inhibition of EZH2 or PI3K/AKT restores afatinib sensitivity.In vivo, combination therapy with an EZH2 inhibitor and afatinib suppresses tumor growth without toxicity.

pmc-12618565.title: Insect vectors have personality: first evidence with the tiger mosquito Aedes albopictus
pmc-12618565.creator: Giulia Cordeschi, Valentina Mastrantonio, Chiara De Nicola, Valentina Lucchesi, Romeo Bellini, Daniele Canestrelli, Daniele Porretta
pmc-12618565.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In recent decades, our view of inter-individual diversity in insects has been deeply impacted by the discovery that they exhibit individual personalities, expressed as consistent individual differences in behavioral tendencies across time and contexts. Personality traits, such as boldness, exploration, and activity, have been documented in several species and linked to variation in multiple life history traits with consequences for insect population ecology. However, personalities remain largely unexplored in mosquito vectors.

pmc-12727524.creator: Yiqing Zhou, Chao Wan, Yichen Xu, Jin Peng Zhou, Kilian Q. Weinberger, Eun-Ah Kim
pmc-12727524.description: As quantum hardware advances toward enabling error-corrected quantum circuits in the near future, the absence of an efficient polynomial-time decoding algorithm for logical circuits presents a critical bottleneck. uslaw-usc-t7-s2271a.title: 7 U.S.C. § 2271a — Advanced marketing training for farmers and ranchers
uslaw-usc-t7-s2271a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t7-s2271a.description: United States Code, Title 7 (Agriculture); Chapter 55 (Department Of Agriculture). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary of Agriculture may establish a program to train farmers and ranchers in advanced techniques for the marketing of agricultural commodities, livestock, and aquacultural products produced by such farmers and ranchers, including (where appropriate as determined by the Secretary) training in the use of futures.
